meta.yt_title: Why an X-ray Can't Show Everything: What It Misses
meta.full_description:
An X-ray is a quick shadow picture that works well for bones and a first look at the chest. It can miss small changes and soft tissues, so doctors sometimes add ultrasound, CT or MRI. This video is for learning only; please discuss your own report with your doctor.

Explained by a radiologist, Dr. Hemakshu V. Chaudhari, D.M.R.E

Educational content only. This is not medical advice and cannot replace a consultation:
please talk to your own doctor about your report.
Visuals are drawn illustrations, not patient images.

A radiologist explains how an X-ray makes its picture and why it shows bone well but soft tissue less clearly. You will also learn why a doctor may suggest an ultrasound, CT or MRI after an X-ray. Always discuss your own report with your doctor.
